scenes.headline: How an agent turns a scene into a glTF
scenes.sub: Construct 1.0: a JSON scene, a checker, an exporter
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Trestle! Construct turns a text scene into a 3D model with moving parts.

scenes.text: A model writes a scene as data, and plain Python does everything after that. The compiler, the checker and the exporter need no key.
scenes.mark: plain Python does everything after that
scenes.say: The model only writes data. Everything after that is ordinary Python, with no key needed.

scenes.title: From a request to a model

steps.say: A model reads your request and writes a scene: named parts, facts, and joints.
A checker validates the scene and reports each problem with a fix.
The exporter writes a glTF with a pivot node for each joint, ready for Blender or an engine.

scenes.title: How a hinge becomes an animation
scenes.say: A joint turns into an animation in four moves.

items.say: Each joint lists the parts it moves.
The exporter adds a pivot node on the hinge line.
It samples a few eased keyframes.
And plays the joints in order groups, one and a half seconds each.

left.title: Needs a model
left.say: A model researches, writes and reviews.

right.title: Plain Python
right.say: Plain Python validates, compiles and exports.

scenes.label: parts in the shipped scenes are marked verified
scenes.say: The scenes label their guesses. Eighty-seven of two thousand nine hundred sixteen parts are marked verified.

scenes.label: gap between the piano's prop tip and its lid
scenes.note: worked out by hand from two joints
scenes.say: Two separate joints on a piano meet within a tenth of a millimetre. Nothing in the checker tests that.

scenes.text: The format keeps every guess labelled and every joint exact, but nothing checks that moving parts still meet.
scenes.mark: nothing checks that moving parts still meet
scenes.say: Check the open pose yourself. The checker will not.
A model writes the scene, Python exports it, and you test the open pose.
